result:
task: Record `gov resources` in the command list the way DEC-542 records a command, and revise the earlier tests that pin the recorded command set so they hold it exactly with `resources` in it.
status: PACKAGES. Commit 173e8e97 is made and W1-32 and W1-07 pass. W1-26 has 2 failures, both `[resources]` cases, because the checks' own command list (`src/gov/check/commands.py`) is outside W2-20's allowed paths (package P-1).
work_completed: Read the ticket, the W2-20 card, DEC-221, DEC-462, DEC-491, DEC-542, DEC-546, DEC-729 and DEC-732, and the four earlier tests named in the brief. Two of them pin the recorded set exactly: `test_w1_07_recorded_commands.py:46` and `test_w1_32_command_set.py:57`. The other two read the list without pinning it: W1-32's set-difference check and W1-26's parametrized cases. I added one line in the form of DEC-542 to `w1_07_support.py`: `RECORDED_GOV_COMMANDS = RECORDED_GOV_COMMANDS + ("resources",)`, with a comment citing DEC-491 and DEC-729. I changed the two pin lines to name `resources`. The set is still exact: W1-32 still fails on any command that is in neither the twelve nor the list. I kept the test names so the README tables still match. Nothing under `src/` was written. I judged that no new owner decision is needed: the owner approved the plan, and with it the KPI that names `gov resources` (DEC-729), and DEC-542 fixes the form of a recorded line (confidence medium).
files_changed: tests/acceptance/W1-07/w1_07_support.py; tests/acceptance/W1-07/test_w1_07_recorded_commands.py; tests/acceptance/W1-32/test_w1_32_command_set.py; tests/acceptance/W2-20/README.md
evidence: Commit 173e8e97 "W2-20 (DAEO-r30l): record gov resources in the command list (DEC-542)", with trailers Task: DAEO-r30l · Role: independent-test-designer · Implements: DEC-729 · Rewrite-Reason: the KPI adds gov resources; the earlier tests hold the recorded set exactly, so resources is recorded in W1-07's command list and W1-07's and W1-32's pins name it · Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5. `git log --oneline -2` shows 173e8e97 (this commit), then 786ffa04 (the engineer's). `git status --short` after the commit printed nothing (clean). The hooks folder holds only `*.sample` files, no `pre-commit`. `gov.__file__` line: `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-20/src/gov/__init__.py`.
tests: W1-32: 81 passed (72.8 s). W1-07: 224 passed (332.9 s); the latency cases of DEC-372 passed this time. W1-26: 2 failed, 412 passed, 1 skipped (339.9 s). The skip was there before: "the full project does not pass gov check yet". Both failures are new `[resources]` cases. (1) `test_a_recorded_command_without_its_module_is_a_finding_that_names_it[resources]`: with the module removed, no `core-commands` finding names `resources`. (2) `test_a_skill_may_name_a_recorded_gov_command[resources]`: the skill validator flags it with "SKILL_UNKNOWN_COMMAND: unknown gov command 'resources'". W2-20's own suite was not run, because I did not touch it.
discoveries: The checks' command list is a separate copy in `src/gov/check/commands.py` (`RECORDED_GOV_COMMANDS = ("ci", "launch", "telemetry")`). Both `core-commands` and the skill validator read it, or a list like it, and it is outside W2-20's allowed paths. So recording a command fully takes this test line plus that list. I found the file name from a grep line only; no implementation was read.
risks: Until P-1 is settled, W2-20's branch carries 2 red cases in W1-26, and a full regression or `gov close` will report them. Leaving `resources` out of W1-26's cases instead would be a loosening and would leave the tests' list and the checks' list disagreeing, so I did not do that.
lessons: A command recorded under DEC-542 lives in two lists: the tests' list (`w1_07_support.py`) and the checks' list (`src/gov/check/commands.py`). A ticket that adds a `gov` command needs that `src` file in its allowed paths. The guard refuses a recursive `grep` over `.` because it reaches the settings file, so search `tests/` and `docs/` by name.
proposed_decisions: P-1. Question: how do the checks' command list and the skill validator come to record `resources`? Why now: the 2 W1-26 failures block W2-20's close. Options: (a) widen W2-20's allowed paths by `src/gov/check/commands.py` (and the validator's list, if the engineer finds it is a separate file), so the engineer adds `"resources"` in one line; (b) a small follow-up ticket for that one line, with W2-20 closing after it; (c) re-baseline W1-26 to hold only DEC-542's four, which is a loosening and leaves the two lists disagreeing. Impact: one line of `src`; W1-26 back to green. Reversible: yes. Cost: small. Recommendation: (a), as a delegated orchestrator decision recorded before the change (DEC-463). Confidence: high.
unresolved: The 2 W1-26 `[resources]` failures until P-1 is decided and applied. The W1-07 and W1-26 READMEs still say "four" recorded commands (outside the lines the brief let me change).
recommended_next_action: The orchestrator decides P-1; under (a), the engineer adds `"resources"` to `src/gov/check/commands.py` and reruns W1-26 to green.
